To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LDL(-) is enriched in esterfied and free cholesterol and in triglycerides and that it induces chemokine release by endothelial cells.

LDL(-) isolated in FH subjects has a composition different from the non-electronegeative fraction, and induces chemokine release by endothelial cells, which may contribute, at least in part, to atherogenesis.
LDL(-) isolated either from FH or NL individuals is enriched in cholesterol and triglycerides, and induces chemokine release by HUVECs, but not the expression of the adhesion molecule VCAM-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the pathogenic role of LDL(-) in atherosclerosis, particularly in FH.
the chemical characterization of LDL(-) in FH subjects and the inflammatory properties of LDL(-) on endothelial cells.
the chemical characterization of LDL(-) of FH subjects and its inflammatory capacity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LDL(-) is a pro-inflammatory LDL subfraction with the potential to contribute to the atherosclerotic process.

LDL(-) is a subpopulation of atherogenic LDL, which is more atherogenic in FH subjects than in NL subjects, and this is probably due to its higher content of apoE, sialic acids and NEFAs, and its greater capacity to induce chemokine release.
the LDL(-) isolated in this study is a heterogeneous fraction, which is enriched in NEFAs, sialic acids, and apoE, and is not associated with increased oxidative stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LDL(-) is not a modified form of LDL but a distinct LDL subfraction that has the ability to promote inflammation.
LDL(-) is enriched in cholesterol and triglycerides, and has increased amounts of NEFAs, apoE, apo C-III and sialic acid.
LDL(-) is a more atherogenic LDL subfraction in FH subjects compared with NL subjects.

LDL(-), a pro-inflammatory subfraction of LDL, is enriched in apoE, apo C-III, siallyglycoconjugates, and NEFAs.
the inflammatory properties of LDL(-) are not related to oxidative modification.
